NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 844 6310 4047, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at LaurenP@RollingHillsEstatesCA.Gov.
  Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for
  their consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 844 6310 4047, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by, COUNCIL MEMBER

  ADJOURN TO PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD MEETING.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

A.  REGULAR PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BOARD OF DIRECTORS MEETING -
  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ANNUAL REPORT

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Community Services Supervisor Morquecho explained that the fiscal year expenditures listed
in the staff report include the annual cross country race, office supplies, and equipment rentals,
in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF. She further explained that due to the established
fiscal year of the Pepper Tree Foundation, the previous year’s Holiday Parade is also included
in the expenditures listed.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA suggested changing the Pepper Tree Foundation’s fiscal year
to align with the City’s fiscal year. She also inquired about the “Other Uses and Interest” listed
on the Statement of Funds balance.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  UPDATED PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BYLAWS

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that the Pepper Tree Foundation Indemnity Agreement
was approved at the October 13, 2020 Joint Pepper Tree Foundation Board meeting.

City Attorney Davis stated that he would discuss the question regarding the Foundation’s fiscal
year with staff and return to the Council with more information.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE THE PROPOSED BYLAWS LANGUAGE, SEPARATING 1.02 FOR
  SEPARATE DISCUSSION AND APPROVAL.

City Attorney suggested tabling the approval of the bylaws language to discuss the purpose
first rather than approving the bylaws without the purpose being included.

Discussion ensued regarding section 1.02 of the bylaws.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted her concerns regarding extending the purpose for the
various issues listed, and the potential of diluting the funding that goes towards parks, trails,

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JANUARY 12, 2021
 open spaces, facilities and recreation programs, which directly impact residents. She also
expressed concern that this could potentially draw elected officials into fundraising.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN stated that bylaws are typically long-term and visionary
documents, and the wider the array of options within the bylaws, the more opportunity in the
long-run to be able to operate within the purpose of the entity. He suggested the Council
consider proceeding by approving the bylaws as presented, and make expenditure decisions
in the future as presented to the Board of Directors.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE THE UPDATED PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BYLAWS AS
  PRESENTED.

Discussion ensued regarding the use of the broader word “programs” within the purpose,
rather than more narrowly defining it. City Attorney Davis suggested using more broad
language as proposed and City Manager Grammer explained that staff’s intention is to
provide the Board with clarity and flexibility within the language.

Discussion ensued regarding the ability of the Board to appoint a Fundraising or
Development Committee, and the ethics of fundraising by elected officials.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA summarized her position, stating that she agrees with
MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN’s summary of the purpose of bylaws, that she has no issues
with section 1.02 as it is currently worded, and believes the Board’s role is to make sure the
Foundation’s money is spent correctly, but also ensure that there is money to be spent. She
then explained the contributions form that can be filed with the FPPC in relation to donations
and fundraising.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN restated his motion, seconded by COUNCIL
  MEMBER STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL
  CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE UPDATED PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION BYLAWS AS
  PRESENTED.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  NOES:  Huff
  ABSENT:  None

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by, MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECONVENE TO CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

C.  PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT UPDATE

Administrative Aide Sinkler provided a presentation of the City’s public engagement over the
last year.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ applauded Administrative Aide Sinkler and staff for their
successful community engagement through all of the platforms used over the past year.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF and MAYOR ZUCKERMAN echoed COUNCIL MEMBER
SCHMITZ’s sentiments regarding staff’s effective communication with the community.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
JANUARY 12, 2021
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA highlighted and recognized the informative City updates being
sent out regularly throughout the pandemic.

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

This item was received and filed by the Council.

11.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  CARES  ACT  SMALL  BUSINESS/NON-PROFIT  ASSISTANCE  GRANT
  DISBURSEMENT - ROUND TWO

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.
No public testimony was received.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered.

B.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

City Manager Grammer provided an update on the Los Angeles County Health Officer Order,
noting that Los Angeles County is consistently reporting more than 10,000 new COVID-19
confirmed cases daily, ICU capacities in the Southern California region remains at 0%, and the
City is currently operating under the State’s December 3 Stay at Home Order. Rolling Hills
Estates’ positive case numbers are on the rise, however the per capita case rate still remain
much lower than County-wide per-capita case rates. Phase one of the vaccine distribution
continues for healthcare workers and those in assisted living facilities, with second phase of 75
years and older and frontline workers to begin in February, followed by those ages 65-74 years
old. There are no City events currently planned for the next few months to report on.

City Manager Grammer explained that City Hall is currently open by appointment only, in
response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN.

12.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

13.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported on the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Health Department Research Group held last week.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF also reported on the League of California Cities Los Angeles
Division meeting held last week, as well her recent appointment to the League’s Community
Services Policy Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ attended the first session of the California Contract Cities
Associations’ (CCCA) Virtual Legislative Tour.

Discussion ensued regarding current housing legislation and the State committees appointed
to monitor local cities legislation regarding housing.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JANUARY 12, 2021

16.  ADJOURNMENT

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO

There being no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN so ordered, at 9:04 P.M. to the next
